Hypothesis: Introduction pathways significantly influence the success of non-native plant species in Catalonia, as indicated by the number of invaded plots. The relationship between minimum residence time (mrt) and invasion success is consistent across different introduction pathways, but the introduction pathway itself has a significant effect on the number of invaded plots. This relationship was found to be statistically significant based on the regression analysis.

4. Data Distribution: Examined the distribution of the minimum residence time (mrt) using a histogram.
5. Relationship Analysis: Explored the relationship between mrt and invasion success metrics (number.of.invaded.plots and area.of.occupancy.10km) using scatter plots.
6. Pathway Analysis: Investigated the relationship between introduction pathways and invasion success using box plots.
7. Regression Analysis: Conducted a multiple linear regression analysis to examine the interaction between mrt and introduction pathways on the number of invaded plots, using one-hot encoding for categorical variables and including interaction terms.
